parts.text: In this experiment, you will determine the density of glass. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 1.1. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) • Measure the length l of the boiling tube provided. l = ..........................................................cm • Measure the external diameter d of the boiling tube. Use the wooden blocks to help you. d = ..........................................................cm [1]

ms.label: 1(a)(ii)
ms.text:
suitable precaution:
e.g. measure in (at least) 2 places (and take average),
avoid lip,
ensure blocks smooth,
no dirt between tube and block

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Assuming that the boiling tube is an approximate cylinder, calculate a value for its external volume V 1 using the equation V 1 = π d 2 l 4 . V 1 = ................................................... cm 3 [1]

parts.label: i
parts.text: (b) (i) • Completely fill the boiling tube with water. • Pour the water from the boiling tube into the measuring cylinder. • Read and record the volume V 2 of the water. V 2 = .................................................. cm 3 [1]

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the volume V 3 of the glass, using the equation V 3 = V 1 – V 2 . V 3 = .................................................. cm 3 [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) • Use the balance to measure the mass m of the boiling tube. m = .............................................................g • Calculate the density ρ of the glass, using the equation ρ = m V 3 . ρ = ............................................................... [2]

ms.label: 1(d)
ms.text:
any reference to why tube is not a cylinder,
tube may contain some water when mass taken,
difficult to fill to brim and then pour out
